text.en: NUMERICAL METHODS ATLAS · PROBLEM A tiny three-center H3+ RHF / MP2 / FCI example Explore this problem’s equations, reference conditions, methods and published code. Saved result figure Demonstrate RHF, MP2 and finite-basis FCI for a tiny fixed three-center H3+ molecule. Independent operator assembly and two-electron RS2 identity qualify this fixed toy. No fresh external PySCF scalar. General molecular DFT, CC, multireference methods, precision energetics, geometry optimization and chemical accuracy remain unimplemented/unverified. MP2 is not variational. Equations and problem definitions Two electrons/3 explicit s orbitals, one fixed non-symmetric triangle. Molecular DFT, CC and general multireference/large molecules remain unimplemented tails. One H3+ geometry[(0,0,0),(1.5,0,0),(.5,1.5,0)]bohr, charge+1,2electrons/3s orbitals; energies in hartree. Stationary electronic Schrödinger equation H^elΨ=EelΨ,Etot=Eel+∑A<BZAZBRAB Fixed-nuclei nonrelativistic electronic eigenproblems; add nuclear repulsion separately. Preserve the existing hydrogenic radial examples. Additional examples are restricted to one-dimensional box/HO and two-electron FCI in at most3AOs, not general many-electron direct solvers or continuum-exact molecules. Closed-shell Hartree–Fock equations F^=h^+∑j∈occ(2J^j−K^j),F^ϕi=εiϕi FC=SCε,C†SC=I Closed-shell occupied-orbital RHF equations include nonlocal exchange. Preserve existing He local-reduction and H2RHF examples. New calculations cover only fixed minimal two-electron H2/H3+ models; UHF equations have their own mapped model. No general multicenter molecules, global open-shell stability, complete-basis or general correlated-method guarantee.
